```
######## EVOGEN vs_our_opening (full) ########
Concrete transferable delta — three things evogen does that v4.py OW_OPENING (v4.py:639-696) and the greedy menu do NOT:

1) MULTI-STEP SEQUENCE SEARCH with captured-planet feedback. Ours is a single-pass greedy: build op_cands once, sort by static gain, then take non-conflicting (src,tgt) pairs in one sweep (v4.py:642-696). Targets are scored independently against the FROZEN initial board; a grab never becomes a new source and never finances the next grab. Evogen's DFS forward-simulates each capture into the state so target B's capture_turn/source/gain are computed AFTER A is owned (evogen1093.py:622-630, 751-761) — it optimizes the joint sequence, not a set of independent one-shots. This is exactly the "ordering" axis our refuted levers never had.

2) TIMED LAUNCH (wait-to-mass at a single source). Ours launches THIS turn or not at all: needed is sized to the ETA-projected defense and must already be affordable (rem[src_id] >= needed) this step (v4.py:666-673, 690-693). Evogen sweeps a wait window, launched = stationed + prod×wait, and will DELAY the launch until one planet alone has accumulated enough to beat the garrison (evogen1093.py:573-575, 598-611), then only emits the move if its scheduled launch_turn equals the current step (evogen1093.py:768-773). That is single-source-but-patient — directly addresses our "多而小 / thin grabs that don't stick": evogen sends one fleet that is provably over the garrison at landing, we send whatever's affordable now.

3) DIFFERENT OBJECTIVE that REWARDS holding. Both use the same per-grab filter prod×(H−eta) − cost > 0 (ours v4.py:679-682; evogen evogen1093.py:719,754) — so single-grab admission is equivalent. The delta is the SELECTION objective: ours picks by that static per-grab gain only; evogen maximizes a board-level opening_score that sums realized future production from ALL planets it will own (evogen1093.py:661-673), so it prefers sequences that compound. Note: OW_OPENING is single-source like evogen's OPENING (so multi-source pooling is NOT the opening delta — that lives in evogen's mid-game plan_target_commitment); the opening delta is sequence-search + timed-mass + a hold-rewarding additive objective.

Caveat for the red-team prior (v4.py:130-138): evogen's opening_score is a SELF-SIDE additive potential, not the conservation-correct differential terminal value. The prior's claim — that a beam over our conservation-terminal value re-derives greedy because the value<=0 gate zeroes concentration's marginal value — does NOT directly refute evogen's design, because evogen never uses that differential terminal value in the opening; it uses an own-production accumulation where earlier/compounded captures have strictly positive marginal value. The transferable hypothesis is therefore: the lever that could beat greedy is not "concentration under our terminal value" (refuted) but "sequence search + timed single-source mass under an own-horizon-production objective" (evogen's actual opening, untested by our 12 levers).

######## INTEGRATION ########

## injection_point
Replace the OPENING block at v4.py:639-696 (gated `if OPENING and step < OPENING_TURNS:` at line 640, returning `op_moves` early at 695-696). That block already sits at the right seam: it runs AFTER the projection/ledger/reserve/launch_budget setup (base_traj/base_arr at 450-451, reserve 484-503, launch_budget 524, defense_need 608-613) but BEFORE the greedy candidate menu (`candidates=[]` at 698) and the hub-and-hammer (849-985). A planner should occupy this same slot: when `step < OPENING_TURNS`, compute a plan and `return plan_moves` to PREEMPT the greedy menu for the opening window; otherwise fall through to the existing greedy/hub-and-hammer for mid/late game. The early-return contract (695-696) is exactly how OPENING hands off, so the planner reuses it. Note the planner must respect `_avail`/`launch_budget`/`reserve` already computed above it, and must emit `[src_id, angle, int(ships)]` move triples (same shape as op_moves at 692 and moves at 1121). The 4p `_term` owner-coding (single `player` vs everyone-else) at 553-558 is unchanged by where you inject. OPENING block structure: per-source × per-target double loop (643-646), iterative size↔eta convergence via `_solve_intercept` (653-669, 3 iters because fleet_speed depends on size), path-block guard (675-678), production-gain score `prod*(OPENING_H-eta)-needed` with `gain<=0` skip (679-683, NO value-gate — the refuted bit), then a greedy non-joint allocation: sort by gain desc (685), walk candidates spending per-source `rem` and marking `taken` targets (689-694).

## value_blindness
The terminal value is `_term` (v4.py:553-558): it reads ONLY position k=H of one planet's owner/ships list and returns +ships if owned by `player`, -ships if enemy, 0 if neutral. A candidate's `value` (783-785) is the H-terminal signed advantage of the two touched planets (replayed via `_replay` at 766-782) MINUS the do-nothing baseline `_base_adv` (560-562, also pure k=H). The `value <= gate` gate (798, gate=0 unless EM) kills anything not net-positive at the single horizon H=26. WHY this is blind to opening tempo/board-control: (1) Frozen-opponent + conservation. The projection is do-nothing for BOTH sides — no enemy reaction is modeled (the capability-prior reserve at 489-497 is the only nod, and it only inflates garrison floors, never the candidate value). So 'deny the opponent this neutral / seize the center first' has no representation: whether I or a do-nothing opponent gets a neutral, the value of MY capture is just my ships there at H minus what I'd have anyway. The red-team verdict (130-138) states this exactly: under conservation, logistics/concentration value == 0, so beam search re-derives the greedy menu. (2) Per-touched-planet additivity. `value` sums `_term` over the source and target planet independently (783); there is no joint board-position term, so 'controlling a contiguous region' or 'opening tempo lead in planet-count' (the ep-80118852 5-vs-7 deficit) is never scored — only this-planet ship arithmetic at H. (3) Single fixed horizon H=26 (PROJ_H, line 42). Opening control is a 40-80 step phenomenon (EM_PHASE=80 line 95; ep median early-phase boundary step 80); at H=26 a neutral grabbed now and a neutral grabbed in 15 turns look near-identical in discounted ship terms, so 'grab the contested ones FIRST / in the right ORDER' is invisible. (4) No discount/tempo term in the gate itself — `signed_adv` in forecast_sim.py:183-195 HAS a gamma=0.97 tempo discount but v4 does NOT use it for gating (it uses raw `_term` at H); so even the available tempo signal is unused. Consequence (the crux): a planner that optimizes `_term`-sum is provably greedy, so the opening planner needs its OWN objective that scores tempo/control/ordering, computed from the same forward sim but NOT collapsed to a single-planet k=H net-ship diff.

## objective_needed
The planner must optimize a multi-step OPENING-CONTROL objective that the conservation-terminal value cannot express, scored over a longer opening horizon Ho (~50-80, cf OPENING_H=50 line 60 / EM_PHASE=80 line 95), evaluated by replaying a candidate SEQUENCE of launches through forecast_sim. Concretely, score a candidate plan P (an ordered set of [src,tgt,turn,ships] launches over the opening) by: (a) PLANET-COUNT / CONTROLLED-PRODUCTION trajectory — at each k in 1..Ho count planets the projection shows me OWNING and sum their `prod` (controlled production rate), integrated with a tempo discount (reuse forecast_sim.signed_adv's gamma=0.97 form, fsim.py:183-195, but applied to controlled-production not net-ship-at-H). This directly targets the ep-80118852 deficit (5 vs 7 planets @ step40, behind in production) that `_term` is blind to. (b) STICK term — penalize captures that the do-nothing projection shows flipping back before Ho (a planet captured at k that `replay_planet` shows enemy-owned by Ho contributes ~0), which credits capture-AND-HOLD sizing without an arbitrary EM_HOLD knob (the refuted T20 lever, 96-99). (c) OPPONENT-DENIAL — a contested neutral (one a nearby enemy source could also reach within Ho) is worth more taken FIRST; compute reachability with the same enemy-ETA logic already in `_exposure` (884-899) and the capability-prior loop (493-496). How to compute from forecast_sim: build the plan's launches as future arrival events `(k_eta, player, ships)` via `_solve_intercept` (344-363) for the launch turn, append them to each touched planet's `base_arr` schedule, and `replay_planet` (fsim.py:90-109) every touched planet to get its owner/ships trajectory; then the objective reads OWNER over ALL k (not just k=H) to integrate controlled-production with discount. The key structural difference from `_term`: read the WHOLE owner-trajectory (control over time), summed across MY planets jointly, not a per-planet k=H net-ship diff. This is what makes the planner non-greedy and not auto-refuted by the red-team argument (130-138).

## reusable
 - _solve_intercept fixed-point ETA/angle solver, v4.py:344-363 (size-dependent fleet_speed converged in 12 iters) — turns a [src,tgt,ships] into (angle, eta, pos); the planner uses it to assign each planned launch an arrival turn
 - _path_blocked sun/planet clip guard, v4.py:366-379 — every planned launch must pass this (the OPENING block already calls it at 675-678)
 - forecast_sim.project, fsim.py:112-180 — bit-exact joint replay of ALL launches issued THIS turn when launches are encoded as synthetic Fleet tuples (id,owner,sx+cos*spd,sy+sin*spd,angle,from,ships); empirically verified to resolve multi-source same-target arrivals at independent ETAs
 - forecast_sim.replay_planet, fsim.py:90-109 — per-planet trajectory from an arrival schedule; the planner appends planned `(eta,player,ships)` events (exactly as the candidate loop does at v4.py:773) and reads the FULL owner list, not just k=H
 - forecast_sim.signed_adv, fsim.py:183-195 — the gamma=0.97 tempo-discounted advantage; reuse its discounted-sum FORM as the planner objective (applied to controlled-production over k) instead of v4's raw k=H _term
 - _safe_surplus capture-floor / threat ledger, v4.py:458-482 — sim-exact max ships sheddable from a source while it stays held through H (binary search, ~9 replays); bounds how much each planned launch may draw from a source
 - _flip_need exact capture-size solver, v4.py:808-847 — min friendly ships arriving at turn K to OWN a target given its do-nothing schedule (handles ties/rank-order via up-to-3 exact replays); the planner uses it to SIZE each opening capture for-hold instead of the refuted EM_HOLD*defender knob
 - reserve / launch_budget / _avail, v4.py:484-524, 633-637 — the planner must spend within these (ledger reserve + phase-scaled in-flight cap); already computed before the injection point
 - _exposure enemy-reachability, v4.py:884-899 and the capability-prior enemy-ETA loop 493-496 — reusable for the opponent-denial / contested-neutral term

## sim_sequence_eval
PARTIALLY, with a caveat that drives the planner design. forecast_sim.project (fsim.py:112-180) jointly + bit-exact replays a SET of launches issued on the CURRENT turn: encode each as a synthetic Fleet tuple and it sweeps movement, swept-collision and combat over H — empirically verified here (two sources onto one target resolved as arrivals at turns 10 and 24, owner flipped correctly; a single 25-ship launch arrived turn 22). BUT project only knows fleets that exist NOW; it does NOT model launches the planner intends to make on FUTURE turns (those fleets don't exist yet). So a true SEQUENCE-over-H (launch at t, then another at t+8, etc.) must be scored one of two ways, both already in the codebase: (A) event-append + replay_planet — compute each planned launch's arrival turn with _solve_intercept (v4.py:344-363) and append `(eta,player,ships)` to each touched planet's base_arr, then replay_planet (fsim.py:90-109) every touched planet; this is precisely the per-candidate scoring at v4.py:766-782, generalized to N launches across the plan. Cost: ~5-7 microseconds per replay_planet call (measured H=26-60), so scoring a plan touching ~8 planets = ~50 us. (B) iterated project — advance the board to the next decision epoch and re-project; ~1.2-1.7 ms per project (measured, H=26-60), so a few epochs per plan = a few ms. (A) is ~20-30x cheaper and bit-consistent with replay_planet's documented project()-equivalence (the self-test at fsim.py:221-233 asserts replay_planet == project per planet). Caveat for fidelity: the event-append path assumes my planned fleets don't collide with each other / the sun en route (guarded by _path_blocked) and does not model the enemy re-routing — acceptable since the planner's objective is explicitly opening-control under a do-nothing-opponent model, same assumption the rest of v4 uses.

## time_budget
Generous headroom. Kaggle hard cap is 1000 ms/turn (VALIDATION.md:14 notes ~20x local margin target; submissions.md:23 worst-case 18.55 ms/turn; README.md:318 ~4 ms/turn typical). Measured here on this box: v4.agent is 0.94 ms (10 planets/8 fleets), 1.62 ms (14/12), 3.62 ms (20/18) — the 18.55 ms figure is a high-planet-count worst case, typical is 1-4 ms. So headroom is ~1000 minus ~4 = ~996 ms/turn, i.e. the opening planner can spend ~100-200x the current per-turn cost and still sit at a comfortable ~5-10x margin. Concrete search affordance using event-append scoring (~5-7 us/replay_planet, ~50 us to score an 8-planet plan): a budget of even 50 ms/turn affords ~1000 full plan evaluations — enough for a real beam/sequence search over the opening (e.g. beam width 20-50 over a depth-3-5 launch sequence with size↔eta re-solve). Because the planner only runs while step < OPENING_TURNS (~25-80 turns of a ~150-step game), the amortized cost over the whole game is small. _solve_intercept (12-iter fixed point) is the main per-candidate cost beyond replay; cap candidate fan-out (sources × reachable contested targets) the way the OPENING loop already bounds it (643-646) to stay well inside budget.

## four_p
The 4p ladder is ~half of games and DOES update rating (~17% net mu; EPISODES.md:101-105), and 4p winning is driven by EARLY neutral-expansion SPEED, not attack share (ep analysis: winners 5.5 planets @ t50 vs losers 2.3; losers eliminated ~t81 — EPISODES.md:108-109). This is directly aligned with the opening planner's controlled-production/planet-count objective, so a tempo-correct opening planner is plausibly the FIRST lever that helps BOTH formats (unlike the 11 refuted single levers, all 2p-tuned). Constraints: (1) The planner must not break 4p byte-equivalence guards — `_term` (553-558) and the capability-prior reserve (493-497) already treat all non-`player` owners as 'enemy' (single coding), which is correct for FFA survival; keep the planner's controlled-production objective owner-agnostic (count MY planets, treat all others as not-mine) so it doesn't need rival-identity. (2) The refuted OW_4P_MODE 'don't be the tall poppy / reduce aggression' lever made things WORSE when we were ahead (1.469→1.719 avg_rank; EPISODES.md:114-117) — so the opening planner should NOT down-weight expansion in 4p; it should expand FASTER (the survival signal), consistent with not breaking 4p. (3) Validate on arena/eval_4p.py (T17 gate: avg_rank / 1st-rate / elimination-rate / t50 planet-count — EPISODES.md:119-120) in addition to the 2p evogen gate, since t50 planet-count is the metric the planner most directly moves. (4) The persistent per-PLAYER state pattern (_V4S keyed by player, v4.py:218, 858) must be honored if the planner keeps cross-turn plan state, to avoid the mirror-seat coupling bug the red-team flagged (216-218).
```

```
RECOMMENDATION: build_minimal_first

RATIONALE: Do NOT build the full planner; build the three offline measurement probes first (super-additivity, objective-divergence, conversion). Rationale: the proposal's ONLY genuine escape from the documented prior is the short-horizon controlled-production objective (the red-team verdict at v4.py:130-138 is explicitly conditioned on the conservation-terminal value, so a non-conservation objective is the one untested axis). Everything else — multi-source, SET+ORDER, capture-and-hold sizing — is a recombination of couplings that are already refuted (OW_MULTISRC, OW_COARRIVAL, OW_OPENING) or whose sizing is monotonic-negative (EM, postmortem 2026-06-16-t20-early-massing.md) and over-defensive (v4f, −9pt). The single highest-value, lowest-cost action is to EMPIRICALLY test the red-team prior rather than re-assert or re-defy it: does a set/order opening search over a production objective actually rank differently from greedy AND have nonzero super-additivity under the engine's conservation dynamics, AND does opening board-control even predict the terminal win at our tier? All three can be answered offline in ~1-2 days reusing forecast_sim.project/replay and the existing OW_LOG/episode pipeline, with zero agent change and zero ladder cost. If any probe fails (and the prior plus the cliff diagnosis — v4 ~1-2% vs kuni05, bottleneck is the cliff not the opening — make failure the strong base rate), we have avoided the 13th refuted lever for the cost of measurement. If all three pass, that is the first hard evidence in 12 levers that the opening is a real, exploitable, non-greedy lever, and THEN a thin frozen-opponent beam (width 3-4, depth 3, opening-only, default-OFF) is justified and gated at the +7pt bar. This is consistent with the project's own measure-first discipline that correctly PARKed T16 below the bar.

## how_it_differs_from_refuted
 "On paper the proposal claims three deltas vs the refuted set, and each is contestable: (1) vs OW_OPENING (v4.py:622-696): OW_OPENING is single-source, no ordering, no hold-sizing, no value gate, scored by per-target production-gain — the proposal adds multi-source + SET + ORDER + capture-and-hold + opponent-awareness. GENUINE delta = the SET+ORDER joint valuation and hold-sizing. BUT the red-team prior (v4.py:130-138) says that exact joint-valuation wrapper is what collapses to greedy / maps onto the refuted couplings, so this delta lands squarely in already-refuted territory unless super-additivity is empirically > 0. (2) vs set-beam (the red-team target): the proposal swaps the objective from conservation-terminal to controlled-production-at-opening-horizon. This is the ONE structurally novel element — the red-team verdict is explicitly conditioned on the conservation-terminal value (under which logistics/concentration value == 0); a production/board-control objective at a SHORT horizon is not conservation-correct and could in principle assign nonzero value to concentration/ordering. This is the only place the proposal can legitimately escape the prior. (3) vs EM (capture-and-hold sizing): EM applied hold-sizing per-grab inside greedy with no set/order; the proposal embeds it in a planner. But EM's refutation was a MECHANISM refutation (monotonic-negative, over-commit), not a config one — wrapping the same over-committing sizing in a planner does not address WHY it over-commits. Net: the proposal is differentiated from the refuted levers ONLY by the short-horizon controlled-production objective; the action space (multi-source/set/order/hold) is a recombination of refuted couplings. The differentiation is real but narrow and entirely load-bearing on the objective being both non-colinear with greedy AND actually exploitable under engine dynamics."

## minimal_viable_version
 "Do NOT build the planner first. Build a MEASUREMENT probe that tests the load-bearing assumption offline, reusing existing primitives — no agent change. Three cheap steps: (1) SUPER-ADDITIVITY PROBE: on logged opening states (step<80) from real games (use the same `_decode_target`/episode pipeline EPISODES.md cites, or freeze opening states from `pool.h2h` games vs evogen), enumerate the greedy menu of reachable neutral grabs and compute, via `forecast_sim.project/replay` (which already give bit-exact joint multi-launch replay over H), the JOINT controlled-production-at-H of the best SET+ORDER vs the sum of greedy independent picks. If joint − greedy ≈ 0 across states, STOP: the planner has nothing greedy doesn't get (red-team prior confirmed empirically, fail fast, ~1 day). (2) OBJECTIVE-DIVERGENCE PROBE: on those same states, check whether ranking grabs by controlled-production-at-opening-H selects a DIFFERENT first 1-3 targets than the conservation-terminal greedy. If the rankings agree, the new objective is colinear → STOP. (3) CONVERSION PROBE: instrument current v4 (OW_LOG already exists, v4.py:148/221) to log opening board-control (controlled production at step 80) and correlate with terminal outcome over ~80 logged games vs evogen+starter; if step-80 board-control does not predict the win, the opening is not the lever. Only if all three probes pass (super-additivity > 0, rankings diverge, board-control predicts) do you build a thin planner: a bounded (beam width ~3-4, depth ~3 grabs) opening-only set/order search over reachable neutrals, opponent-frozen first (add 1-ply response ONLY after a frozen version shows signal, to avoid the v4f trap), gated behind OW_OPLAN default-OFF, byte-identical when off. The minimal planner reuses `_solve_intercept`, `_flip_need`, `project`, `replay` — no new sim."

## validation_plan
 "Isolate the OPENING effect specifically, not just net win-rate. (1) GATE: paired-seed h2h vs evogen1093 (the proven discriminating mid-tier gate, ~20% v4 baseline), >=150 seeds = 300 games (+-3.5pt 95% CI), via `arena/pool.h2h` with OW_OPLAN overrides on the candidate side only (opponent ignores OW_* — pool.py:46-52). Bake bar = +7pt over the baseline arm (same bar that baked t14, INS-002). (2) NO-REGRESS: starter >=85% AND must NOT exceed baseline starter win-rate by more than noise (the over-defensive tell). (3) CLIFF REFERENCE: vs multifocus/kuni05 (~1240) as a tracker — expect ~no gradient at our tier, but watch for the rare case it moves (would be the real prize). (4) OPENING-ISOLATION (the key differentiator from a blind win-rate A/B): run the SAME candidate with the planner clamped to step<80 only (its design) vs a SHAM arm where the planner is allowed to run all-game — if the all-game arm is no worse, the 'opening' framing is not what's acting; and instrument OW_LOG to confirm the planner actually FIRES different opening sets than greedy (count divergent opening decisions/game) so a null is provably 'fired-and-failed' not 'never-engaged' (the v4a lesson: prove the precondition is met). (5) PAIRED-SEED powered: report w-l-t per arm with CI; treat any |delta| < ~5.5pt at 40 seeds as smoke needing the 150-seed confirm (the v4c +8.3pt-smoke-was-noise lesson). (6) 4p gate: `arena/eval_4p.py` avg_rank/1st-rate/elim-by-t50 must not regress (standing directive)."

## why_might_fail
 - THE RED-TEAM PRIOR IS ABOUT THE SEARCH SPACE, NOT THE VALUE FN, AND THE PROPOSAL DOES NOT ESCAPE IT. v4.py:130-138 says a beam over SET+ORDER of grabs collapses to greedy *because the per-move couplings (co-arrival, multi-source, ordering) map 1:1 onto the refuted levers*. The proposal explicitly re-introduces exactly those couplings (SET+ORDER, multi-source, capture-and-hold sizing). Swapping the OBJECTIVE from conservation-terminal to 'controlled-production at horizon' does not change that the only DEGREES OF FREEDOM the planner has are the same couplings already proven inert (OW_MULTISRC, OW_COARRIVAL +3pt-only, OW_OPENING). A new objective on the same action space can re-rank but the menu it picks from is unchanged.
 - CONTROLLED-PRODUCTION AT AN OPENING HORIZON IS NEARLY COLINEAR WITH WHAT OW_OPENING ALREADY OPTIMIZED. OW_OPENING (v4.py:679-681) scores `prod_by_id[tgt] * (OPENING_H - eta) - needed` = production won over the horizon minus ship cost. 'Controlled-production at horizon H' is the same quantity aggregated over a set. The set/order wrapper is the only delta, and the set wrapper is the refuted beam. So the objective is not new and the wrapper is refuted — high risk of being OW_OPENING with a sort.
 - EM ALREADY TESTED 'OPENING-ONLY + CAPTURE-AND-HOLD SIZING + GATE-SLACK' AND IT WAS MONOTONIC-NEGATIVE WITH NO POSITIVE REGION (postmortem 2026-06-16-t20-early-massing.md: −7.5 to −13.8pt vs evogen; gentlest config −1.2 ≈ noise). The proposal's 'each grab sized to capture-AND-hold' is byte-for-byte the EM mechanism (v4.py:743-744 `needed += EM_HOLD*defender` + EM_SLACK gate at :797). Heavier opening grabs over-commit and LOSE the ship-accumulation race. The proposal must explain why a SET of EM-sized grabs avoids the over-commit that a single EM-sized grab caused — and bigger sets commit MORE ships earlier, the wrong direction.
 - THE CLIFF DIAGNOSIS SAYS THE BOTTLENECK IS NOT THE OPENING MECHANISM. The overkill-revival postmortem (lines 67-71) and EPISODES.md #1 (lines 64-70) both conclude: v4 sits at ~1-2% vs kuni05 because 'we can't reach the board states where concentration matters — the bottleneck is the cliff itself, not a missing lever.' If the opening is not where the strong tier actually pulls away in a way our value can act on, a better opening planner optimizes a sub-game whose advantage is dissipated by the mid-game cliff. The ep-80118852 evidence is a 4p FFA WE WON against collapsing rivals (insights.md:36-42), not a 1v1 loss vs the strong tier — it is weak evidence that the OPENING is the 1v1 cliff cause.
 - OPPONENT-AWARENESS IS THE EXACT FAILURE MODE OF v4f. v4f relaxed frozen-opponent with a 1-ply best response and regressed −9pt by going over-defensive (beat weak starter MORE, 94 vs 91%, lost to evogen by trading passively — postmortem lines 59-63). Any 'opponent-aware' opening valuation that models enemy retakes will, under the same dynamics, make the agent hold/over-garrison and lose the ship race. The proposal inherits v4f's failure surface.
 - MEASUREMENT POWER vs THE RIGHT TIER. evogen (~1093) is the discriminating gate that the suite saturates above; but the CLIFF the proposal targets is the strong tier (multifocus/kuni05 ~1240) where v4 floors at ~1% with NO GRADIENT (v4_overkill_ab.py:57-58). A +Npt vs evogen does not prove cliff escape, and the strong tier gives no measurable signal — so the validation that matters most is the one with the least power.
 - OPENING WINDOW (step<80) IS ~HALF THE GAME AT OUR TIER. Diagnostic in overkill-revival round 2 (lines 21-27): median game vs evogen is ~152 steps, only 2/10 reach step 200. A 'step<80' opening planner governs the majority of a 152-step game, so 'replace greedy ONLY during the opening' is not a small scoped change — it is replacing the allocator for half the games we play, raising blast radius and regression risk.

## must_be_true
 - The opening planner's OBJECTIVE must be provably NON-COLINEAR with both (a) the conservation-terminal value (else red-team prior: collapses to greedy) AND (b) OW_OPENING's production-gain-minus-cost (else it is OW_OPENING with a sort). Concretely: 'controlled-production / board-control at horizon H' must, on logged opening states, rank target SETS differently from a greedy production-gain sort in a way that is decision-relevant (different first 1-3 grabs), not just a different scalar.
 - The value of ORDER+SET must be real and NOT decomposable into independent per-grab decisions. The whole premise of a SET+ORDER planner is that the joint value of grabbing {A then B then C} exceeds the sum of greedy independent grabs (sequencing frees a source, a held A defends B, etc.). If this super-additivity is ~0 under the engine's conservation dynamics — which the red-team verdict asserts it is — the planner has nothing to optimize that greedy doesn't already get. This must be MEASURED (super-additivity > 0) before any build.
 - Heavier capture-and-hold sizing must NOT recreate EM's over-commit. The planner must demonstrably commit LESS or EQUAL total ships in the opening than the greedy baseline while controlling MORE production — i.e. it wins by ORDERING/TARGETING, not by sending more ships. If it sends more ships earlier it is EM and is already refuted monotonic-negative.
 - It must NOT go over-defensive against weak opponents. The diagnostic tell for both v4f and EM was beating starter MORE while losing to the gate (postmortem). The candidate must hold starter win-rate ~flat (no over-defensive bump) AND raise the gate win-rate — a one-sided weak-tier gain is the refutation signature.
 - The opening advantage must SURVIVE to game end. Given games end ~152 steps and the opening is step<80, a board-control lead at step 80 must convert to a terminal win, not be dissipated by the mid/late greedy phase. This requires showing that opening board-control at step 80 is causally predictive of the terminal outcome on logged games — otherwise the planner optimizes a leading indicator that does not pay out.
 - There must be a board state our agent can actually REACH where the opening planner's choices matter against the strong tier. The cliff diagnosis (v4 ~1% vs kuni05) implies we may be eliminated/dominated before the opening choices compound. Must be true that vs the strong tier we are still competitive through step 80 (planet count within ~1-2, ship parity) — else the opening is moot.

## kill_criteria
 - Super-additivity probe: median (best-set joint controlled-production − sum of greedy independent picks) over logged opening states is within noise of 0 (e.g. < 5% of the greedy value). KILL — this is the red-team prior empirically confirmed; the planner reduces to greedy.
 - Objective-divergence probe: the controlled-production-at-opening-H ranking picks the same first 1-3 targets as the conservation-terminal greedy on >~80% of logged states. KILL — the new objective is colinear, the planner is OW_OPENING with a re-sort.
 - Conversion probe: opening board-control at step 80 has no/weak correlation (e.g. |r| < ~0.2 or AUC < ~0.6) with terminal win over logged games. KILL — the opening is not the cliff lever; optimizing it cannot move the terminal result.
 - Over-defensive tell: in any A/B, the candidate beats starter MORE than baseline while NOT raising the evogen gate. KILL — this is the exact v4f/EM refutation signature (one-sided weak-tier gain).
 - Monotonicity tell: a small sweep of the planner's hold-margin / depth shows the candidate getting WORSE as it does MORE (deeper/heavier), with no positive region. KILL — this is the EM/OVERKILL monotonic-negative signature; do not parameter-search (= refuted OW_* random search anti-pattern).
 - Gate A/B: candidate does not clear +7pt vs evogen on >=150 paired seeds (the bake bar that baked t14 and caught a prior regression). KILL — record as the 13th refuted lever, keep default-OFF.
 - 4p no-regress: candidate's 4p avg_rank degrades vs baseline (~1.78) on eval_4p. KILL or at minimum block-ship (standing 2p+4p directive).
```

```markdown
# Scope — integrated opening-sequence planner (T20 follow-on)

> orbit5, 2026-06-16. Grounded in `orbit_wars.py`, `agent/versions/v4.py`,
> `agent/versions/suite/evogen1093.py`, `forecast_sim.py`, and a 3-agent study
> (evogen reverse-engineering + v4 integration + adversarial red-team).
> **Bottom line: build the 3 measurement probes FIRST, not the planner.** The probes
> are the cheapest way to get the first hard evidence in 12 levers about whether the
> opening is a real, non-greedy, win-predictive lever. Strong base rate of failure.

## 1. Problem & the ONE genuine escape axis
- The cliff: ~100% vs weak, **0–20% vs strong** (evogen 1093 / multifocus / kuni05 1240); v4 ladders ~700.
- Episode 80118852 (our kuni05): opening is **多而小** — early ≤step80 median launch ~20 ships, we trail in planet count (5 vs 7 @ step40), mass only late.
- **12 single-mechanism levers refuted** (OW_OVERKILL, OW_MULTISRC, OW_COARRIVAL, OW_OPENING, v4a/f/c/i, T20 OW_EM). 
- 🔑 **Red-team prior (`v4.py:130-138`, 2026-06-12):** set/beam planning over the **conservation-correct terminal value** provably **re-derives the greedy menu** — under conservation, concentration/coordination/ordering have **zero marginal value** (the `value<=0` gate kills them); a beam's couplings map 1:1 onto the refuted levers.
- **The one untested axis:** evogen's opening does **not** use the conservation-terminal value. It optimizes an **own-side additive horizon-production accumulation** (`opening_score`, evogen1093.py:661-673) under which **earlier/compounded captures have strictly positive marginal value**. A planner on *that* objective is the single element of the proposal not auto-refuted by the prior. Everything else (set/order, multi-source, capture-and-hold sizing) is a recombination of refuted couplings.

## 2. Reference — what evogen actually does (cited)
- **Branch-and-bound DFS over capture SEQUENCES** (evogen1093.py:738-763), run **only the first 3 env steps** (`OPENING_TURNS=3`, :68, :811-812); per-turn greedy after.
- **Objective `opening_score`** (:661-673): Σ over planets I'll own of `stationed + prod·(H−turn)` + in-flight landing garrisons. Monotone-additive, **no enemy/conservation term** → ordering compounds.
- **Captured-planet feedback** (:622-630, :751-761): a grab becomes a new source AND its production finances the next grab; target B's capture-turn/source/gain are recomputed *after* A is owned.
- **Timed single-source mass** (:573-575, :598-611): waits, `launched = stationed + prod·wait`, launches only when one source alone beats the garrison at landing — directly fixes "thin grabs that don't stick."
- **Optimistic-bound pruning** (:728-736, :743-744) over a small pre-sorted positive-gain candidate set → tiny tree, sub-budget.
- **Transferable delta vs our `OW_OPENING` (v4.py:639-696):** SET+ORDER joint valuation + timed-mass + the **hold-rewarding additive objective**. (Note: evogen's *opening* is single-source — multi-source pooling is its *mid-game* `plan_target_commitment` :349-479 — so multi-source is **not** the opening delta.)

## 3. The crux — why our value fn can't express this
`_term` (v4.py:553-558) reads only `k=H` of one planet's owner/ships: `+mine / −enemy / 0 neutral`; candidate `value` (783-785) sums it over the two touched planets minus the do-nothing baseline; `value<=0` gate (798). It is **blind** to: (a) **opponent-denial** (frozen do-nothing opponent — taking a contested neutral first has no representation); (b) **board-position/region control** (per-planet additive, no joint board term — the 5-vs-7 planet deficit is unscored); (c) **tempo** (single fixed `H=26`; a grab now vs in 15 turns look identical; `signed_adv`'s γ=0.97 discount, fsim.py:183-195, is **unused** in the gate). ⇒ a planner optimizing `_term` is provably greedy. The opening planner needs its **own** objective reading the **whole owner-trajectory** (control over time) summed jointly across my planets.

## 4. Proposed design — IF (and only if) §5 probes pass
- **Injection:** replace the `OPENING` block (v4.py:639-696, `if OPLAN and step < OPEN_WIN: ... return plan_moves`), preempting the greedy menu for the opening window only; fall through to greedy + hub-and-hammer after. Gated **`OW_OPLAN` default-OFF, byte-identical when off.** Emit `[src,angle,int(ships)]`; respect `_avail`/`launch_budget`/`reserve` computed above (484-524).
- **Objective (the novel element):** controlled-production trajectory over `Ho≈50–80`: at each `k` count planets the projection shows me **owning**, sum their `prod`, integrate with a **tempo discount** (reuse `signed_adv`'s γ form, applied to controlled-production not net-ship-at-H). Plus a **STICK** term (a capture that `replay_planet` shows flipping back before `Ho` contributes ~0 — credits hold without the refuted `EM_HOLD` knob) and an **opponent-denial** term (contested neutrals — reachable by a nearby enemy source within `Ho` via `_exposure` :884-899 — worth more taken first). **Owner-agnostic** (count MY planets, all others "not-mine") → 4p-safe.
- **Search:** thin **frozen-opponent beam, width ~3–4, depth ~3 grabs**, opening-only. Score a plan by **event-append + `replay_planet`**: assign each planned launch an arrival turn via `_solve_intercept`, append `(eta,player,ships)` to each touched planet's `base_arr`, `replay_planet` every touched planet, read the full owner list. ~5–7 µs/replay → ~50 µs/plan → **~1000 plans in 50 ms** (budget ~996 ms headroom; v4 typical 1–4 ms/turn). Opponent-aware term added **only after** a frozen version shows signal (avoid the v4f trap).
- **Sizing:** capture-for-hold via **`_flip_need`** (exact min ships to own at K, v4.py:808-847), **not** `EM_HOLD·defender`. Hard constraint: **commit ≤ greedy total opening ships** — win by ordering/targeting, not by sending more (else it is EM, monotonic-negative).
- **Reuse (no new sim):** `_solve_intercept`, `_path_blocked`, `project`/`replay_planet`, `signed_adv`, `_safe_surplus`, `_flip_need`, `reserve`/`launch_budget`, `_exposure`. Honor per-player state (`_V4S`, :218) to avoid the mirror-seat bug.

## 5. ⛔ Measure-first gate — 3 offline probes BEFORE any agent change
Per the project's measure-first discipline (correctly PARKed T16). All offline, reuse `forecast_sim.project/replay` + `OW_LOG`/episode pipeline, **zero agent change, zero ladder cost, ~1–2 days**.
| Probe | Question | KILL if |
|---|---|---|
| **P1 Super-additivity** | best SET+ORDER controlled-production vs Σ greedy independent picks, on logged opening states | joint − greedy ≈ 0 (<5%) → red-team prior confirmed; planner = greedy |
| **P2 Objective-divergence** | does controlled-production-at-`Ho` pick different first 1–3 targets than the conservation greedy? | rankings agree >80% → objective colinear; planner = OW_OPENING-with-a-sort |
| **P3 Conversion** | does step-80 board-control predict the terminal win over ~80 logged games (vs evogen+starter)? | \|r\|<0.2 / AUC<0.6 → opening isn't the cliff lever |
**Only if all 3 pass** is the thin planner (§4) justified.

## 6. Validation — IF built
- **Gate:** vs evogen ≥150 paired seeds (300 games, ±3.5pt), **+7pt bake bar** (the bar that baked t14, caught a regression). 
- **No-regress:** starter ≥85% AND **not** a one-sided weak-tier bump (the v4f/EM over-defensive tell). **4p:** `eval_4p` avg_rank/1st-rate/elim-by-t50 no worse than baseline (~1.78). **Cliff ref:** multifocus/kuni05 tracker (expect no gradient).
- **Opening-isolation:** clamp-to-opening arm vs a sham all-game arm (if all-game is no worse, the "opening" framing isn't what's acting); `OW_LOG` count of divergent opening decisions/game (prove it FIRES — the v4a lesson).
- **Kill at any:** over-defensive tell · monotonic-negative param sweep (do NOT parameter-search — refuted anti-pattern) · <+7pt at 150 seeds → record as the **13th refuted lever**, default-OFF.

## 7. Risks (why it is likely the 13th refuted lever)
1. The action space (set/order/multi-source/hold) is refuted couplings; only the objective is novel — narrow and entirely load-bearing on P1/P2.
2. Controlled-production-at-H is **nearly colinear** with OW_OPENING's `prod·(H−eta)−cost` (v4.py:679-681) — the set wrapper may be all that differs, and that wrapper is the refuted beam.
3. Capture-for-hold is the **EM mechanism**, monotonic-negative (over-commit); a *set* of hold-sized grabs commits MORE ships earlier — the wrong direction.
4. **Cliff diagnosis** (overkill-revival postmortem, EPISODES.md #1): v4 floors ~1–2% vs kuni05 because we can't reach the board states where it matters — the bottleneck may be mid-game, not the opening. The ep-80118852 evidence is a **4p win vs collapsing rivals**, weak for the 1v1 cliff cause.
5. Opponent-awareness is **v4f's exact failure surface** (−9pt over-defensive) — add it only after a frozen version shows signal.
6. **Measurement power:** evogen has discriminating power but the real cliff (kuni05) has none — the validation that matters most is the weakest.

## 8. Effort, phasing, deadline
- **Phase 0 — probes (§5):** ~1–2 days, offline. Decision gate: all 3 pass → Phase 1; any fail → STOP, record measured-then-parked (like T16/T8/relay). **Fits before the 2026-06-23 deadline.**
- **Phase 1 — thin frozen planner (§4):** ~2–3 days build + 150-seed gate. Default-OFF.
- **Phase 2 — only if Phase 1 clears +7pt:** opponent-denial term, 4p tuning, ladder submission. ~3–4 days.
- **Total ~1–1.5 weeks IF the probes pass** (does NOT fit before 2026-06-23); ~1–2 days if they kill it (the likely outcome). Pre-deadline, **only Phase 0 is feasible** — the full planner is a post-deadline / final-eval-window effort.

## 9. Recommendation
**`build_minimal_first`** — build the 3 probes (Phase 0), not the planner. They empirically test the red-team prior (super-additivity, objective-divergence, conversion) instead of re-asserting or re-defying it, at ~1–2 days and zero ladder cost. If any fails (the strong base rate), we avoid the 13th refuted lever for the cost of measurement. If all pass, that is the first hard evidence in 12 levers that the opening is a real exploitable non-greedy lever — and the thin frozen planner is then justified at the +7pt bar. Keep v4 (~700) on the ladder and kuni05 (1079.7) + coarr as anchors throughout.
```

```python
"""Phase 0 — three offline probes that decide whether the integrated opening planner
is worth building (designs/2026-06-16-opening-planner-scope.md). Zero agent change,
zero ladder cost. Reuses v4's exact _solve_intercept/_path_blocked and forecast_sim.

  P1 super-additivity : does a SET+ORDER search (captured-planet feedback, budget-
                        respecting) beat the GREEDY selection on controlled-production
                        at the opening horizon Ho?  KILL if median gain < 5%.
  P2 objective-divergence : does ranking grabs by controlled-production pick different
                        first-3 targets than the conservation-terminal (_term) greedy?
                        KILL if mean agreement > 80% (objective colinear).
  P3 conversion       : does our board-control at step 80 predict the terminal win
                        over logged games?  KILL if |point-biserial r| < 0.2.

Usage:
  python arena/opening_probes.py --selftest
  python arena/opening_probes.py --games 40 --procs 20
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import math
import os
import sys

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
COMP = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(HERE, ".."))
V = os.path.join(COMP, "agent", "versions")
sys.path.insert(0, V)
# opponent (gitignored in this worktree) — fall back to the main checkout
MAIN_V = os.path.expanduser("~/test/tt_pangu/competitions/orbit-wars/agent/versions")
EVO = os.path.join(V, "suite", "evogen1093.py")
if not os.path.exists(EVO):
    EVO = os.path.join(MAIN_V, "suite", "evogen1093.py")
V4 = os.path.join(V, "v4.py")

import forecast_sim as fs  # noqa: E402
import v4 as v4mod  # noqa: E402  (module-level _solve_intercept/_predict_pos/_path_blocked)

GAMMA = 0.97
HO = 60  # opening control horizon
OPEN_STEPS = (20, 40)  # states for P1/P2
CTRL_STEP = 80  # state for P3


# ---------- board helpers ----------
def _obs_tuples(obs):
    planets = [tuple(p) for p in obs["planets"]]  # (id,owner,x,y,r,ships,prod)
    fleets = [tuple(f) for f in obs.get("fleets", [])]
    init_by_id = {p[0]: tuple(p) for p in obs["initial_planets"]}
    return planets, fleets, init_by_id, obs["angular_velocity"], int(obs["step"]), set(
        obs.get("comet_planet_ids", []) or []
    )


def _controlled_production(owner_by_pid, prod_by_pid, me):
    """Σ_k γ^k Σ_p prod_p·[owner_k==me] over the trajectories (each owner list len Ho+1)."""
    total = 0.0
    g = 1.0
    for k in range(1, HO + 1):
        g *= GAMMA
        s = 0.0
        for pid, o in owner_by_pid.items():
            if o[k] == me:
                s += prod_by_pid[pid]
        total += g * s
    return total


def _candidate_grabs(planets, fleets, init_by_id, ang_vel, step, comet_ids, me, base_traj):
    """Reachable NEUTRAL grabs from our sources: best (min-eta) source per neutral,
    sized to the projected defender+1. Returns list of dicts."""
    mine = [p for p in planets if p[1] == me]
    neutrals = [p for p in planets if p[1] == -1 and p[0] not in comet_ids]
    cands = []
    for tgt in neutrals:
        best = None
        for src in mine:
            ships_guess = max(1, int(tgt[5]) + 1)
            sol = None
            needed = ships_guess
            eta_k = 1
            for _ in range(3):
                sol = v4mod._solve_intercept(
                    src[2], src[3], tgt[0], ships_guess, step, init_by_id, ang_vel
                )
                if sol is None:
                    break
                _, t_ticks, _ = sol
                eta_k = max(1, min(int(t_ticks), HO))
                bt = base_traj.get(tgt[0])
                defender = bt["ships"][eta_k] if bt is not None else tgt[5]
                needed = int(defender) + 1
                if needed == ships_guess:
                    break
                ships_guess = needed
            if sol is None:
                continue
            angle, t_ticks, pos = sol
            if t_ticks > HO:
                continue
            if v4mod._path_blocked(
                src[2], src[3], pos[0], pos[1], src[0], tgt[0], planets, comet_ids
            ):
                continue
            if best is None or eta_k < best["eta"]:
                best = {"tgt": tgt[0], "src": src[0], "ships": int(needed), "eta": eta_k,
                        "angle": angle, "prod": tgt[6]}
        if best is not None:
            cands.append(best)
    return cands


def _eval_plan(plan, planets, fleets, init_by_id, ang_vel, step, comet_ids, me, base_traj, base_arr):
    """Controlled-production at Ho for executing `plan` (list of grab dicts), evaluated
    jointly: debit each source, add each target's arrival, replay touched planets, use
    base trajectory for the rest."""
    owner0 = {p[0]: p[1] for p in planets}
    ships0 = {p[0]: float(p[5]) for p in planets}
    prod = {p[0]: p[6] for p in planets}
    debit = {}
    arr_add = {}
    for g in plan:
        debit[g["src"]] = debit.get(g["src"], 0.0) + g["ships"]
        arr_add.setdefault(g["tgt"], []).append((g["eta"], me, float(g["ships"])))
    touched = set(debit) | set(arr_add)
    owner_by = {}
    for pid in base_traj:
        if pid in touched:
            arrs = list(base_arr.get(pid, []))
            arrs += arr_add.get(pid, [])
            o, _s = fs.replay_planet(owner0[pid], ships0[pid] - debit.get(pid, 0.0),
                                     prod[pid], arrs, HO)
            owner_by[pid] = o
        else:
            owner_by[pid] = base_traj[pid]["owner"]
    return _controlled_production(owner_by, prod, me)


def _term_value(grab, planets, init_by_id, me, base_traj, base_arr):
    """The v4 conservation-terminal differential value of a single grab (k=HO net-ship,
    +mine -enemy, source debited + target arrival vs do-nothing baseline)."""
    owner0 = {p[0]: p[1] for p in planets}
    ships0 = {p[0]: float(p[5]) for p in planets}
    prod = {p[0]: p[6] for p in planets}

    def term(o, s):
        k = HO
        return s[k] if o[k] == me else (-s[k] if o[k] != -1 else 0.0)

    def base_adv(pid):
        bt = base_traj[pid]
        return term(bt["owner"], bt["ships"])

    so, ss = fs.replay_planet(owner0[grab["src"]], ships0[grab["src"]] - grab["ships"],
                              prod[grab["src"]], base_arr.get(grab["src"], []), HO)
    tarr = list(base_arr.get(grab["tgt"], [])) + [(grab["eta"], me, float(grab["ships"]))]
    to, ts = fs.replay_planet(owner0[grab["tgt"]], ships0[grab["tgt"]],
                              prod[grab["tgt"]], tarr, HO)
    return (term(so, ss) + term(to, ts)) - (base_adv(grab["src"]) + base_adv(grab["tgt"]))


def _greedy_select(cands, planets, me, key):
    """v4-style: rank by `key`, take non-conflicting (each source budget, each target once)."""
    ships_avail = {p[0]: float(p[5]) for p in planets if p[1] == me}
    ranked = sorted(cands, key=key, reverse=True)
    sel = []
    for g in ranked:
        if g["ships"] <= ships_avail.get(g["src"], 0):
            sel.append(g)
            ships_avail[g["src"]] -= g["ships"]
    return sel


def _search_best(cands, planets, fleets, init_by_id, ang_vel, step, comet_ids, me,
                 base_traj, base_arr, depth=3, beam=6):
    """Beam search over SET+ORDER of grabs (budget-respecting), maximizing controlled
    production. Captured-planet feedback is implicit in the joint replay (a held target
    contributes its production; source contention is enforced by the ship budget)."""
    ships_avail0 = {p[0]: float(p[5]) for p in planets if p[1] == me}
    # state: (plan_list, remaining_avail dict, cp)
    init = ([], dict(ships_avail0), _eval_plan([], planets, fleets, init_by_id, ang_vel,
                                               step, comet_ids, me, base_traj, base_arr))
    frontier = [init]
    best = init
    for _d in range(depth):
        nxt = []
        for plan, avail, _cp in frontier:
            used_t = {g["tgt"] for g in plan}
            for g in cands:
                if g["tgt"] in used_t or g["ships"] > avail.get(g["src"], 0):
                    continue
                np_ = plan + [g]
                na = dict(avail)
                na[g["src"]] -= g["ships"]
                cp = _eval_plan(np_, planets, fleets, init_by_id, ang_vel, step,
                                comet_ids, me, base_traj, base_arr)
                nxt.append((np_, na, cp))
                if cp > best[2]:
                    best = (np_, na, cp)
        if not nxt:
            break
        nxt.sort(key=lambda x: x[2], reverse=True)
        frontier = nxt[:beam]
    return best


# ---------- data generation ----------
def _run_game(seed, opp):
    from kaggle_environments import make
    env = make("orbit_wars", configuration={"seed": seed})
    env.run([V4, opp])
    steps = env.steps
    rew = [s["reward"] for s in steps[-1]]
    rec = {"seed": seed, "reward0": rew[0], "reward1": rew[1], "n": len(steps)}
    for tag, st in (("s20", 20), ("s40", 40), ("s80", CTRL_STEP)):
        idx = st if st < len(steps) else len(steps) - 1
        rec[tag] = steps[idx][0]["observation"]
    return rec


def _gen(seeds, opp, procs):
    from multiprocessing import Pool
    with Pool(procs) as p:
        return p.starmap(_run_game, [(s, opp) for s in seeds])


# ---------- probes ----------
def _state_probe(obs, me=0):
    planets, fleets, init_by_id, ang_vel, step, comet_ids = _obs_tuples(obs)
    base_traj, base_arr = fs.project(planets, fleets, ang_vel, init_by_id, step, HO,
                                     comet_ids=comet_ids)
    cands = _candidate_grabs(planets, fleets, init_by_id, ang_vel, step, comet_ids, me, base_traj)
    if len(cands) < 2:
        return None
    cp_indep = {g["tgt"]: _eval_plan([g], planets, fleets, init_by_id, ang_vel, step,
                                     comet_ids, me, base_traj, base_arr)
                - _eval_plan([], planets, fleets, init_by_id, ang_vel, step, comet_ids,
                             me, base_traj, base_arr)
                for g in cands}
    greedy_sel = _greedy_select(cands, planets, me, key=lambda g: cp_indep[g["tgt"]])
    cp_greedy = _eval_plan(greedy_sel, planets, fleets, init_by_id, ang_vel, step,
                           comet_ids, me, base_traj, base_arr)
    _plan, _av, cp_search = _search_best(cands, planets, fleets, init_by_id, ang_vel,
                                         step, comet_ids, me, base_traj, base_arr)
    super_add = (cp_search - cp_greedy) / cp_greedy if cp_greedy > 1e-9 else 0.0
    # P2: first-3 by CP vs by conservation _term
    by_cp = [g["tgt"] for g in sorted(cands, key=lambda g: cp_indep[g["tgt"]], reverse=True)[:3]]
    tvals = {g["tgt"]: _term_value(g, planets, init_by_id, me, base_traj, base_arr) for g in cands}
    by_term = [g["tgt"] for g in sorted(cands, key=lambda g: tvals[g["tgt"]], reverse=True)[:3]]
    agree = len(set(by_cp) & set(by_term)) / max(1, len(by_cp))
    return {"super_add": super_add, "agree": agree, "ncand": len(cands),
            "cp_greedy": cp_greedy, "cp_search": cp_search}


def _board_control(obs, me=0):
    planets = obs["planets"]
    return sum(p[6] for p in planets if p[1] == me), sum(1 for p in planets if p[1] == me)


def _point_biserial(xs, ys):
    n = len(xs)
    mx = sum(xs) / n
    sx = (sum((x - mx) ** 2 for x in xs) / n) ** 0.5
    my = sum(ys) / n
    sy = (sum((y - my) ** 2 for y in ys) / n) ** 0.5
    if sx < 1e-9 or sy < 1e-9:
        return 0.0
    cov = sum((x - mx) * (y - my) for x, y in zip(xs, ys)) / n
    return cov / (sx * sy)


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--games", type=int, default=40)
    ap.add_argument("--starter-games", type=int, default=20)
    ap.add_argument("--procs", type=int, default=20)
    ap.add_argument("--seed0", type=int, default=50000)
    ap.add_argument("--selftest", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    if args.selftest:
        recs = _gen([args.seed0, args.seed0 + 1], EVO, 2)
        print("selftest games:", [(r["seed"], r["reward0"], r["n"]) for r in recs])
        for r in recs:
            for tag in ("s20", "s40"):
                pr = _state_probe(r[tag])
                print(f"  {r['seed']} {tag}: {pr}")
        return

    evo = _gen(list(range(args.seed0, args.seed0 + args.games)), EVO, args.procs)
    sta = _gen(list(range(args.seed0, args.seed0 + args.starter_games)), "starter", args.procs)
    print(f"games: evogen={len(evo)} (won {sum(1 for r in evo if r['reward0'] > r['reward1'])}), "
          f"starter={len(sta)} (won {sum(1 for r in sta if r['reward0'] > r['reward1'])})", flush=True)

    # P1 + P2 over opening states (evogen games)
    sadds, agrees = [], []
    for r in evo:
        for tag in ("s20", "s40"):
            pr = _state_probe(r[tag])
            if pr:
                sadds.append(pr["super_add"])
                agrees.append(pr["agree"])
    sadds.sort()
    med_sa = sadds[len(sadds) // 2] if sadds else 0.0
    mean_ag = sum(agrees) / len(agrees) if agrees else 1.0
    print(f"\nP1 super-additivity: n={len(sadds)} states | median Δ(search vs greedy)={med_sa * 100:+.1f}% "
          f"| mean={sum(sadds) / max(1, len(sadds)) * 100:+.1f}% | frac>5%={sum(1 for x in sadds if x > 0.05) / max(1, len(sadds)) * 100:.0f}%")
    print(f"   VERDICT: {'KILL (search ≈ greedy → planner redundant)' if med_sa < 0.05 else 'PASS (search beats greedy ≥5%)'}")
    print(f"\nP2 objective-divergence: n={len(agrees)} states | mean first-3 agreement(CP vs _term)={mean_ag * 100:.0f}%")
    print(f"   VERDICT: {'KILL (objectives colinear → OW_OPENING-with-a-sort)' if mean_ag > 0.80 else 'PASS (CP ranks differently)'}")

    # P3 conversion over all games: board-control@80 vs win
    xs, ys = [], []
    for r in (evo + sta):
        prodc, _cnt = _board_control(r["s80"])
        xs.append(prodc)
        ys.append(1.0 if r["reward0"] > r["reward1"] else 0.0)
    # evogen-only (the discriminating tier)
    xe, ye = [], []
    for r in evo:
        prodc, _cnt = _board_control(r["s80"])
        xe.append(prodc)
        ye.append(1.0 if r["reward0"] > r["reward1"] else 0.0)
    r_all = _point_biserial(xs, ys)
    r_evo = _point_biserial(xe, ye) if len(set(ye)) > 1 else float("nan")
    print(f"\nP3 conversion: control@80 vs win | r(all {len(xs)})={r_all:+.2f} | r(evogen {len(xe)})={r_evo:+.2f} "
          f"| evogen wins={int(sum(ye))}/{len(ye)}")
    print(f"   VERDICT: {'KILL (control@80 does not predict win)' if abs(r_all) < 0.2 else 'PASS (control@80 predicts win)'}")
    print("\n=== PROBES COMPLETE ===")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

```
def _predict_pos(pid, future_step, init_by_id, ang_vel):
    """Exact predicted (x, y) of a planet at an absolute game step.

    Static planets never move (return initial == current position). Orbiting
    planets rotate at constant angular velocity about the center.
    """
    ip = init_by_id.get(pid)
    if ip is None:
        return None
    ix, iy, r_planet = ip[2], ip[3], ip[4]
    dx, dy = ix - CENTER, iy - CENTER
    orb = math.hypot(dx, dy)
    if orb + r_planet < ROTATION_RADIUS_LIMIT:
        a = math.atan2(dy, dx) + ang_vel * future_step
        return (CENTER + orb * math.cos(a), CENTER + orb * math.sin(a))
    return (ix, iy)
```

````markdown
# Task: Research kuni05-class source, matchmaking behavior, and Kaggle identity mapping

## Mission

Before building the next Orbit Wars architecture, establish the ground truth for three operational questions:

1. Can we download or inspect a public `kuni05` / kuni05-class agent source to study integrated-system design?
2. Does Kaggle assign opponents randomly, by similar skill, by weak-to-strong curriculum, or by another observable pattern?
3. How do we reliably map Kaggle `username`, profile/display name, team name, leaderboard row, submission id, and replay `TeamNames`?

This is a research/docs task only. Do not change agent code. Do not submit. Do not push kernels.

## Read first

- `competitions/orbit-wars/README.md`
- `competitions/orbit-wars/tracking.md`
- `competitions/orbit-wars/submissions.md`
- `competitions/orbit-wars/EPISODES.md`
- `competitions/orbit-wars/ops/episode_discover.py`
- `competitions/orbit-wars/ops/track_submission.py`
- `competitions/orbit-wars/ops/episode_analyze.py`
- `competitions/orbit-wars/ops/kaggle_auth.py`
- `competitions/orbit-wars/references.md`

## Research topic A — public kuni05-class source

Search Kaggle Code/discussions/read-only sources for public kuni05-class Orbit Wars agents, especially:

```text
kuni05/lb-1240-5-orbit-wars-producer-agent-submission
```

Allowed read-only commands, if credentials are available:

```bash
kaggle kernels pull kuni05/lb-1240-5-orbit-wars-producer-agent-submission \
  -p competitions/orbit-wars/sources/kuni05_producer_agent -m
```

Rules:

- Pull only public code/notebook source and metadata.
- Do not submit or push anything.
- Do not vendor large generated outputs.
- Preserve license/attribution notes.
- If source is public and usable, create a system-study summary; do not blindly copy it into our from-scratch agent.
- If reused for an attributed submission, clearly label it as attributed public source, not our own from-scratch agent.

Create/update:

```text
competitions/orbit-wars/discussions/YYYY-MM-DD-kuni05-system-study.md
competitions/orbit-wars/references.md
competitions/orbit-wars/tasks.md
competitions/orbit-wars/tracking.md
```

The system-study summary should answer:

- What files/classes/functions define the agent architecture?
- Is it rules/search/model/hybrid?
- How does it represent battlefield state?
- How does it choose targets and ship sizes?
- Does it have a landing/path oracle?
- Does it do multi-source scheduling, hub-and-hammer, defense ledger, supply chain, or endgame banking?
- What is safe to learn conceptually without copying?
- What needs attribution if reused?

## Research topic B — opponent assignment / matchmaking behavior

Investigate official and empirical evidence for matchmaking.

Official evidence:

- Kaggle competition overview / docs statements about simulation competitions and skill rating.
- Orbit Wars overview/rules if accessible.
- Kaggle docs about submissions playing episodes against agents with similar skill rating.

Empirical evidence:

Use `EpisodeService/ListEpisodes` through existing tooling if possible:

```bash
python competitions/orbit-wars/ops/episode_discover.py --submission-id <known_submission_id>
python competitions/orbit-wars/ops/track_submission.py --once --submission-id <known_submission_id> --decide-after 10 --max 20
```

For several known submissions, collect:

- episode order by id/time if available;
- number of 2p/4p matches;
- initialScore and updatedScore for our submission;
- opponent initialScore distribution;
- opponent names/profile names;
- whether first episodes are systematically weak, similar, or mixed;
- whether assignment becomes closer to current μ over time;
- whether 4p games also update μ.

Deliver a cautious conclusion:

```text
official_matching_rule: similar_skill | random | unknown
empirical_initial_behavior: weak_first | similar_first | mixed | unknown
confidence: low | medium | high
operational_policy: how the ladder loop should interpret first 10/20 episodes
```

Do not overstate if evidence is incomplete.

## Research topic C — player identity mapping

Investigate and document how to map:

```text
Kaggle username / account alias
profile display name
team name
leaderboard display
submission id
EpisodeService agents[].submissionId
replay info.TeamNames[seat]
replay rewards[seat]
```

```

competitions/orbit-wars/references.md
competitions/orbit-wars/EPISODES.md
competitions/orbit-wars/insights.md
```

The identity map should include:

```md
| account alias | Kaggle username | profile/display name | team name / replay name | evidence | notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
```

If a profile name is inferred by reward matching rather than direct API identity, mark it as inferred and include evidence.

## Credential and secret policy

You may use `.vscode/.env.harry` and `.vscode/.env.may` only for read-only Kaggle queries if needed.

- No agent code is changed.
- No Kaggle submit/kernel push/dataset upload is performed.
- No secrets are exposed.

## Stop conditions

Stop if:

- credentials would need to be exposed;
- Kaggle public source is inaccessible and no local evidence can answer the question;
- a required action would modify agent code;
- a required action would submit/push/upload;
- source identity remains too ambiguous and could cause false attribution.

- public source availability and path/blocker;
- matchmaking conclusion and confidence;
- identity map conclusion;
- files modified;
- read-only commands run;
- follow-up tasks created;
- risks and next steps.
````

> Excellent. Now I have comprehensive coverage of the system. Let me create the study document based on my analysis:
> 
> ---
> 
> ## KUNI05 PRODUCER AGENT (LB 1240.5) — SYSTEM STUDY
> 
> **Public Kernel ID**: `kuni05/lb-1240-5-orbit-wars-producer-agent-submission` (ID: 121702304)  
> **Author**: kuni05 (from kernel metadata)  
> **Requires**: PyTorch (torch import at main.py:19)
> 
> ---
> 
> ### 1. Agent Architecture & Module Map
> 
> The agent is a **rules-based single-size planner** implemented as a pure PyTorch operator-graph (no neural networks). Architecture:
> 
> | Module | Purpose | Key Functions |
> |--------|---------|---------------|
> | **main.py:360–367** | Entry point | `agent(obs)` – wraps observation, calls runtime, converts sparse payload to moves |
> | **main.py:265–301** | Turn pipeline | `run_turn()` – orchestrates full decision: movement cache, distance cache, garrison status, planning, emission |
> | **main.py:120–262** | Wave planner | `plan_lite_waves()` – scores one-candidate-per-(source,target) pairs, greedily selects up to 6 waves/turn, plans regroup |
> | **planner_core.py:54–111** | Scoring engine | `make_launch_set()`, `score_candidates()`, `competitive_score()` – wraps exact flow-diff scorer |
> | **garrison_launch.py:311–450** | Flow projector | `sparse_launch_flow_delta()` – computes per-player net-ship-delta (production−combat) if a launch fires |
> | **intercept_aim.py:35–154** | Aiming | `intercept_angle()` – continuous fixed-point solver for orbital intercept, analytic first-contact verification |
> | **movement.py:70–433** | Prediction cache | `PlanetMovement` – 20-turn forward position oracle, garrison projection (do-nothing baseline), fleet tracking |
> | **planner_core.py:237–361** | Reachability | `reachable_mask()` – swept-segment distance precheck (strict superset of viability) |
> | **planner_core.py:437–541** | Regroup planner | `_plan_regroup()` – pressure-gradient marshalling of leftover ships to stressed planets |
> | **adapter.py** | I/O | Converts dict observation ↔ tensors and sparse launches → move list |
> 
> **Type**: **Hybrid rules+flow** – hand-written scoring rules (safe_drain, capture_floor, friendly_flip detection) composed with an **exact simulation oracle** (sparse_launch_flow_delta) for candidate evaluation.
> 
> ---
> 
> ### 2. Paradigm: Rules + Exact Forward Model
> 
> **Not a learned policy.** The agent uses torch for:
> - **Vectorized tensor algebra** (not weights): all operations are algebraic with no `nn.Linear`, `nn.Conv`, or learnable parameters.
> - **Exact game physics** mirrors (garrison recurrence, combat survivors, production accounting).
> 
> **Evidence**:
> - No `torch.nn` imports; no `model.parameters()` or gradient updates.
> - `competitive_score()` at planner_core.py:75–86 is a pure arithmetic combination: `me − opp`.
> - `sparse_launch_flow_delta()` at garrison_launch.py:311–450 runs an exact **mini-recurrence** per affected planet over the horizon, mirroring the engine's production→combat step by step (garrison_launch.py:120–151, `_run_exact_recurrence`).
> 
> ---
> 
> ### 3. Battlefield State Representation
> 
> **Observation Parsing** (obs.py:98–100):
> - `ParsedObs` dataclass with per-planet tensors `[P]`: alive, x, y, r, ships, prod, owner_abs.
> - Relative ownership masks (owned, is_enemy, is_neutral) derived from player_id.
> - Orbital parameters (orb_r, orb_a0, is_orbiting) reconstructed from initial_planets.
> 
> **Movement Cache** (movement.py:70–204):
> - `PlanetMovement` predicts `x[k]`, `y[k]`, `alive_by_step[k]` for k ∈ [0, H].
> - Uses observed positions at k=0,1 to infer orbiting planets' angular velocity (movement.py, orbit_phase_index_from_obs_step at aiming.py:7–16).
> - Static planets' future positions trivial; orbiting planets solved analytically from `R`, `a0`, `ω` (intercept_aim.py:81–89).
> 
> **Garrison Status** (movement.py:375–433):
> - `PlanetGarrisonStatus` (owner, ships per step) is a **do-nothing projection**: assumes the agent launches nothing, fleets already in flight resolve deterministically.
> - `garrison_status()` returns post-combat state at each step, plus optional `arrivals_by_owner[P, H, A]` (per-step per-player inbound fleet buckets).
> - Projection uses exact recurrence (garrison_launch.py:83–151): production credited to owner entering step, combat resolved (top1 − top2), ties annihilate.
> 
> **Distance Cache** (distance_cache.py:49–74):
> - `cross_dist[k, s, t]` = Euclidean distance(s@step=0, t@step=k).
> - Precomputed `[K+1, P, P]` for horizon-window lookups, accounts for orbital motion.
> - Used by target shortlist builder to rank enemy/neutral targets by proximity.
> 
> ---
> 
> ### 4. Target & Ship-Size Selection
> 
> **Target Shortlist** (planner_core.py:271–295):
> 1. **Offensive targets** (up to 12 by config): enemy/neutral planets ranked by minimum cross-distance to owned sources (proximity; descending, ties broken by ascending slot index for device determinism at planner_core.py:126–138).
> 2. **Defensive targets** (up to 4): friendly planets projected to flip within horizon H, ranked by urgency = `prod·(H − flip_turn) + garrison_now` (ship-mass units, highest first).
> 3. Combined, no overlap (separate caps).
> 
> **Ship Size Selection** (main.py:168–171, **single-size only**):
> - All candidates for a pair (src, tgt) use the **same fleet size**: `safe_drain(src)` (max garrison the source can shed).
> - `safe_drain()` at planner_core.py:587–633: closed-form min of projected garrison over held turns within horizon H. Mathematically: over turns t ∈ [1, H] where src is still mine, the largest amount removable now s.t. garrison stays ≥ 0 every turn is min_t(ships_traj[t]).
> - Floor: `capture_floor[T, K]` at planner_core.py:186–232: per-target, per-arrival-turn.
>   - Owned targets: floor = 1 (reinforcement, no capture needed).
>   - Enemy/neutral: floor = ceil(defenders_at_k + 1.0 overhead).
>   - If sends < floor_at_arrival: gated as invalid.
> 
> **Viability Gates** (main.py:182–211):
> 1. Strict-superset reachability (planner_core.py:298–360): swept-segment point-to-distance from source@0 to target's path over [0, K]. Precheck before expensive intercept solver.
> 2. Intercept angle solve (intercept_aim.py:35–154): continuous root-finding (fixed-point iteration, 6 iterations) for orbital intercept time t* matching fleet speed and target orbit. Analytic first-contact screen (intercept_aim.py:157–287) checks exact sweep collision vs. all planets, sun, OOB on the path; ties broken by lowest slot.
> 3. ETA cap: uniform K_eta = min(config.horizon, status.ships.shape[-1] − 1); arrival turn k ≤ K_eta.
> 
> ---
> 
> ### 5. Landing/Path Oracle & Collision Avoidance
> 
> **Intercept Aim** (intercept_aim.py:35–154):
> - **Continuous intercept solver**: Analytic orbit model. Target at t=0: (x0, y0); at t=1: (x1, y1). Derives orbital centre R, phase a0, angular velocity ω (intercept_aim.py:81–84).
> - Target position at time t: `(CENTER + R·cos(a0 + ω·t), CENTER + R·sin(a0 + ω·t))`.
> - Solves: `speed·t = dist(target_pos(t), source) − gap` via fixed-point iteration (6 iterations, intercept_aim.py:97–100).
> - **No grid scan**: continuous t*, not a discrete step lookup. Converges because target radial speed << fleet speed for reachable shots.
> 
> **First-Contact Verification** (intercept_aim.py:157–287):
> - Engine-faithful deterministic verdict: swept-pair collision (line segment from fleet start to end) vs. every step-0-alive planet, sun, OOB.
> - Two-phase:
>   1. **Broad phase** (intercept_aim.py:221–227): AABB cull (segment bounding box vs. planet swept box inflated by radius). Drops planets that can never be hit → keeps ~1-3 planets for typical clear shot.
>   2. **Narrow phase** (intercept_aim.py:241–287): exact swept-pair collision detector (`_swept_pair_hit_mask` at movement_aiming.py:43–70) on kept shortlist, chunked for memory (byte-budgeted, no OOM).
> - Lowest-slot same-step tie-break (intercept_aim.py:266): if multiple planets hit at the same step, use lowest slot index → CPU≡CUDA determinism.
> - **Result**: contact_planet == target → viable; else non-viable (eta = ∞).
> 
> ---
> 
> ### 6. Advanced Strategy Modules
> 
> **Safe Drain** (planner_core.py:587–633):
> - Answers: "How many ships can source shed now while staying held over H?"
> - Closed form, no scoring: min of projected garrison over held turns. Doomed sources (lose planet before H) can shed all ships.
> - Used to cap max launch size per source.
> 
> **Capture Floor** (planner_core.py:186–232):
> - Per-target, per-arrival-turn (k=1..K) defense threshold.
> - Owned target: floor = 1 (no capture).
> - Enemy: floor = ceil(projected_garrison_at_k + 1.0).
> - Launch must satisfy size ≥ floor_at_arrival_turn to pass gate.
> 
> **Friendly Flip Detection** (planner_core.py:244–268):
> - Identifies owned planets the do-nothing projection shows flipping to enemy control within H.
> - Urgency = remaining production + current garrison → prioritize defensive sends to planets losing soonest.
> - Ranked as defensive targets (up to 4 per turn).
> 
> **Regroup Marshalling** (planner_core.py:437–541):
> - Post-attack: allocates leftover ships at sources to nearby stressed owned targets.
> - Leftover per-source comes from greedy selection residuals (planner_core.py:410–422: per-source budget tracking).
> - Destinations: owned, alive planets, sorted by cheap_enemy_pressure (main.py:89–117).
> - `cheap_enemy_pressure[P]`: sum of distance-decayed enemy garrisons reachable within horizon; (1 − d/(v·H))₊ decay.
> - Regroup waves: capped at max_regroup_time (6 turns, config), require arrival-turn ownership check, gap > 0.25 pressure delta, scored by (pressure_delta − time_penalty·eta).
> 
> **Multi-Wave Greedy Selection** (planner_core.py:363–434):
> - Builds candidates: one per (source, target) pair; single size = safe_drain.
> - Scores via competitive flow diff.
> - Greedy loop: each iteration picks the best-scored unvetoed candidate (score > roi_threshold = 1.5).
> - **Role mutex** (planner_core.py:385–391): planet cannot both source an attack AND receive a reinforcement in same turn. Prevents double-dipping.
> - Budget tracking: per-source residual ships shrink as contributors are selected.
> - Output: up to W=6 attacks + regroup waves (separate, post-attack).
> 
> ---
> 
> ### 7. Forward Model & Horizon
> 
> **Horizon H** (main.py:59): 
> - Config `horizon=18` (2P default); `horizon=13` (4P config).
> - Defines: projection depth, ETA cap, regroup timing window, safe_drain lookback.
> 
> **Forward Simulation** (garrison_launch.py:83–151, `_run_exact_recurrence`):
> - Steps: k=1..H.
> - Each step: production credited to owner at step start; combat resolved (arrivals vs. garrison, top1−top2 survivor rule); end-of-step death reset.
> - Returns: (owner, ships, pre_combat_owner, pre_combat_ships) each `[N, P, H+1]`.
> - Used by `sparse_launch_flow_delta()` to compute per-player ship flow deltas only for affected planets (source debit, target credit), avoiding dense `[C, P, H, A]` allocation.
> 
> **Sparse Flow Projector** (garrison_launch.py:311–450):
> - Hypothesis: "If I launch these fleets, how do net-ship flows (production − combat losses) change per player?"
> - Avoids dense `[C, P, H, A]` by recomputing recurrence only for planets touched by launches (~2 per candidate). Untouched planets contribute zero delta.
> - Exact mirrors engine rules; no approximation.
> - Result: `[C, A]` per-player delta (hypothetical − baseline). Competitive score: `me_delta − sum(opp_delta)` (planner_core.py:75–86).
> 
> **No search beyond horizon**: The agent does not plan past H. Launches are scored on immediate horizon window only; no nested look-ahead or value iteration.
> 
> ---
> 
> ### 8. Learning & Conceptual Reuse Guidance
> 
> **DO NOT need attribution** (purely conceptual / rules):
> - Safe-drain sizing algorithm (closed-form min projection).
> - Capture-floor mechanics (defender overhead + ownership check).
> - Friendly-flip urgency scoring (production × remaining_turns + garrison).
> - Pressure-gradient regroup idea (centralize defensively under stress).
> - Greedy multi-wave selection with role mutex (don't source and receive same turn).
> - Competitive flow-diff scoring (my gain − opponent gain).
> 
> **REQUIRE attribution if exact algorithm reused**:
> - **Sparse launch flow projector** (garrison_launch.py:311–450): unique exact-only-affected-planets technique. Exact sparse recurrence by (candidate, planet) cell is load-bearing for scalability.
> - **Continuous intercept solver** (intercept_aim.py:35–100): fixed-point iteration on analytic orbit; 6 iterations. If copied line-for-line, cite.
> - **Analytic first-contact** (intercept_aim.py:157–287): swept-pair collision over all planets, sun, OOB, lowest-slot tie-break, byte-budgeted chunking for memory. Engine-faithful reproduce requires exact implementation.
> - **Safe-drain closed form** (planner_core.py:587–633): min over held turns in trajectory. Clever, worth citing if copied.
> 
> **Conceptually sound** (can learn from, adapt freely):
> - The idea of a flow-diff oracle (what-if-I-launch) is standard in game AI; the sparse implementation is the novel part.
> - Reachability precheck (reachable_mask) is a proven technique (broad-phase AABB, narrow-phase exact). Both phases are common patterns.
> - Pressure-decay distance metric for defensive priority is straightforward.
>

```bash
$ cd /home/harry/test/tt_pangu/competitions/orbit-wars
~/.venvs/orbit-wars/bin/python - <<'PY' 2>&1 | grep -vi "open_spiel\|: INFO\|litellm"
import sys; sys.path.insert(0,"ops")
import episode_discover as ed
import statistics as st
for sub, name in [(53582503,"kuni05/flyingfox(harry)"), (53730511,"v4(harry)")]:
    eps = ed.list_episodes(sub)
    # order by episode id (proxy for time)
    eps = sorted(eps, key=lambda e: e["id"])
    rows=[]
    for e in eps:
        ags=e.get("agents",[])
        me=next((a for a in ags if a.get("submissionId")==sub),None)
        if not me: continue
```
